result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edges_str_repr()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edges as formatted string representations. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3371-L3513){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edges_str_repr(limit=1000, use_labels=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns edge representations as strings showing node identifiers with arrow notation. The format depends on whether the graph is directed or undirected: - directed graphs: "source->target" - undirected graphs: "source--target" ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of edge strings to return. Pass `None` to return all edges (warning: may be slow for large graphs). Default limit of `1000` prevents performance issues when working with large graphs. [use_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, preferentially use node labels instead of IDs. Falls back to node IDs when labels are not available for a node. If `False`, always use node IDs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge strings with arrow notation indicating direction. Uses node IDs by default, or labels when `use_labels=True` and available. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Get formatted edges with node IDs: ::: {#9b928621 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Returns ['1->2', '2->3'] graph.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1->2', '2->3'] ``` ::: ::: Get formatted edges with labels: ::: {#7710ba5a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Returns ['A->B', 'B->C'] graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A->B', 'B->C'] ``` ::: ::: Undirected graphs use double dashes: ::: {#5bc09718 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y") ) # Returns ['1--2'] graph.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['1--2'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#42e75550 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns ['X--Y'] graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['X--Y'] ``` ::: ::: Mixed labels (some nodes have labels, others don't): ::: {#579637d9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") # Add node with label ) # Get the node IDs to create an edge alice_id = graph.get_id_from_label(label="Alice") bob_id = graph.get_id_from_label(label="Bob") graph.add_edge(source=alice_id, target=bob_id) # Returns ['Alice--Bob'] graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['Alice--Bob'] ``` ::: ::: Get all edges regardless of size: ::: {#7ca3fd30 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): graph.add_node(label=f"Node_{i}") for i in range(4): graph.add_edge(source=f"Node_{i}", target=f"Node_{i+1}") # Use None to get all edges (may be slow for large graphs!) all_edges = graph.get_edges_str_repr(limit=None, use_labels=True) # Returns 4 len(all_edges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
